title: Convolution tensor descends to finite filtered homotopy localizations
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ be the homotopy category of uniformly finite decreasing filtered cochain complexes of $R$-modules and $W$ its graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. Let $\mathcal G_f(R)$ be its full subcategory of good complexes [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement]: their underlying, filtration-step and graded terms are flat, and their underlying, step and graded complexes are K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Put $\mathcal D_f(R)=\mathcal H_f(R)[W^{-1}]$, localization meaning formal inversion of $W$. Use the signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for the one-point ringed site with ring $R$, and the convolution filtration and canonical graded comparison of [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison].
Convolution tensor on good complexes descends to a bifunctor
$$\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]\times\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}].$$
Transport along the good-replacement equivalence gives a bifunctor $\star:\mathcal D_f(R)\times\mathcal D_f(R)\to\mathcal D_f(R)$. Forgetting the filtration gives a functor $\omega:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$ and a natural isomorphism
$$\omega(U\star V)\cong\omega U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\omega V,$$
where the right side is the ordinary derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$. For each $a$ the representative-level graded comparison descends to a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{gr}^a(U\star V)\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iU\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jV$$
in $D(R)$, for all morphisms of both localized variables. The sum is finite. On a pair of maps between good representatives these comparisons are the canonical maps induced by tensoring representatives and passing to their quotient classes; in particular the underlying morphism is the ordinary derived tensor of their underlying morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0H7Y (proposition-kunneth-filtered), convolution construction preceding Tag 0H7W (lemma-kunneth-converges), with Tag 0H7X (lemma-resolution-filtered-complex); explicit homotopy/localization extension of those constructions. Derived Categories Tag 05S2 (definition-filtered-derived).

proof.text: For good filtered complexes $P,Q$, put $B(P,Q)=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ with the convolution filtration in the statement. By [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison], this filtration is uniformly finite and its underlying, step and graded modules are flat and its underlying, step and graded complexes are K-flat. Thus $B(P,Q)$ is again good. For filtered chain maps $u,v$, set $B(u,v)(x\otimes y)=u(x)\otimes v(y)$. The same cited statement supplies filtration preservation and simultaneous naturality of the canonical graded comparisons. The tensor-map formula preserves identities and composition on generators, so this is a bifunctor on good filtered complexes before passing to homotopies.

source.place: Tag 0H7Y (proposition-kunneth-filtered), convolution and graded comparison preceding Tag 0H7W (lemma-kunneth-converges)

proof.text: We check explicitly that this bifunctor passes to the homotopy classes of [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. If $u-u'=dh+hd$ is a filtered homotopy and $v$ is a filtered chain map, define $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes v(y)$. For $\deg x=p$, the two mixed terms in $dH+Hd$ have coefficients $(-1)^{p-1}$ and $(-1)^p$ and cancel; the remaining terms give $(u-u')(x)\otimes v(y)$. If $v-v'=dk+kd$, use $J(x\otimes y)=(-1)^p u(x)\otimes k(y)$: the terms involving $d_Px$ cancel and the remainder is $u(x)\otimes(v-v')(y)$. These computations use precisely the signed differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Both homotopies preserve convolution filtration since $h,k,u,v$ preserve each factor's filtration step. Adding the two homotopies handles simultaneous changes of representatives. Hence $B$ induces a bifunctor $\mathcal G_f(R)\times\mathcal G_f(R)\to\mathcal G_f(R)$, and the representative-level comparisons are still natural on these homotopy classes.

source.place: Definition 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); explicit signed tensor-homotopy calculation for the filtered homotopies in the discussion before Derived Categories Definition 05S2

proof.text: Write $L:\mathcal G_f(R)\to\overline{\mathcal G}=\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]$. Graded quasi-isomorphisms contain identities. By [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison], if $u,v\in W$ then $B(u,v)\in W$; this includes $(u,1)$ and $(1,v)$. Thus $LB$ inverts every pair in $W\times W$. Apply [lem-sfb-product-localization] to the two factors $L$: $L\times L$ is a localization at $W\times W$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now factors $LB$ through $L\times L$, giving $\overline B:\overline{\mathcal G}\times\overline{\mathcal G}\to\overline{\mathcal G}$ with its specified comparison to $LB$. In the formal-inversion model its value on $(Lu,Lv)$ is $L B(u,v)$, and on an inverse denominator it is the inverse of this map. No functorial choice of resolutions has been used.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), universal property; finite-product and natural-transformation extensions supplied by the cited Mathlib leaves

proof.text: By [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement] the inclusion induces an equivalence $E:\overline{\mathcal G}\simeq\mathcal D_f(R)$. Choose a quasi-inverse $S$ and its unit and counit. Define $U\star V=E\overline B(SU,SV)$ and define its maps by the same composite of functors. The unit of the equivalence identifies $(EP)\star(EQ)$ with $E\overline B(P,Q)$, naturally in localized good objects $P,Q$. This proves the asserted transport. A different quasi-inverse gives the same construction up to the natural isomorphism obtained by inserting the unit and counit; the statement requires a bifunctor, not a functorial free resolution.

source.place: Tag 0H7X (lemma-resolution-filtered-complex); use of the good-replacement equivalence stated in the cited node

proof.text: To descend forgetting the filtration, let $u:K\to K'$ represent an element of $W$. Choose common finite bounds $a<b$ for the two filtrations. Descend from $r=b$, where both steps are zero. The short exact sequences $0\to F^{r+1}K\to F^rK\to\operatorname{gr}^rK\to0$ and their primed analogues give natural long exact sequences by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact, lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]. Assuming $F^{r+1}u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, their five consecutive terms $A=H^{n-1}(\operatorname{gr}^rK)$, $B=H^n(F^{r+1}K)$, $C=H^n(F^rK)$, $D=H^n(\operatorname{gr}^rK)$, $E_0=H^{n+1}(F^{r+1}K)$ have bijective vertical maps except possibly at $C$. For injectivity, $c$ mapping to zero has zero image in $D$ and equals the image of some $b\in B$. The image $b'$ lies in the image of $A'$; lift its preimage through $A\simeq A'$ and subtract its image from $b$. The result maps to zero in $B'$, hence is zero, so $c=0$. For surjectivity, lift the image in $D'$ of $c'\in C'$ through $D\simeq D'$. Its image in $E_0$ is zero by injectivity there, so it lifts to $c\in C$. The difference $c'-u(c)$ comes from $B'$ and can be corrected using $B\simeq B'$. Thus $F^ru$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Finite induction reaches $F^aK=K$, proving that the underlying $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, with no cochain-degree bound.

source.place: Tag 05S3 (lemma-filtered-derived-functors), forgetful-functor argument, specialized to uniform finite bounds; long exact sequence is Homology Tag 0117

proof.text: Forgetting a filtered homotopy gives an ordinary homotopy, and restricting it to a filtration step and then quotienting gives a homotopy on each associated graded complex [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. Consequently forgetting and each $\operatorname{gr}^a$, followed by the ordinary derived quotient, define functors $\mathcal H_f(R)\to D(R)$. The first inverts $W$ by Step 5 and the latter do so by the definition of $W$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore produces $\omega:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$ and $\operatorname{gr}^a:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$ with their canonical representative identifications. Restricting these functors along $E$ gives the corresponding underlying and graded functors on $\overline{\mathcal G}$.

On good pairs, the underlying comparison of [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison] identifies the underlying $B(P,Q)$ with $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$ in $D(R)$, naturally for both chain maps. Its ordinary derived tensor is the one in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$: the identity K-flat resolution of $P$ computes it, and the second-variable transformation is represented by $1_P\otimes v$. Hence for a pair $u,v$ the resulting map is represented by $u\otimes v$, by factoring the pair as $(u,1)$ followed by $(1,v)$. Step 2 shows invariance under homotopies. These are therefore a natural isomorphism between the two functors on $\mathcal G_f(R)\times\mathcal G_f(R)$ obtained by restricting $\omega E\overline B$ and the ordinary derived tensor of the underlying objects. Both invert $W\times W$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the product localization of Step 3 to descend this natural isomorphism to all of $\overline{\mathcal G}\times\overline{\mathcal G}$, with the same representative formula.

source.place: Convolution construction before Tag 0H7W and Tag 0H7Y; ordinary K-flat tensor is Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side

proof.text: Fix $a$. On good representatives use the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison], oriented as $\operatorname{gr}^a B(P,Q)\simeq\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ$. Both sides are functors on the homotopy category: Step 2 and quotienting its filtered homotopies show this for the comparison. The right side is a finite biproduct on each pair of objects, because only the finite nonzero graded ranges can contribute. For a map between pairs, take the union of their finite supports and use the direct sum of the graded tensor maps, inserting zero summands as needed. Enlarging the finite support inserts only zero objects, so the resulting map is independent of it; componentwise composition gives the functor laws. For $u,v\in W$, every summand map is an isomorphism, so this functor inverts $W\times W$. The left side does too by Steps 3 and 6. The cited comparison is simultaneously natural on representatives. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] and [lem-sfb-product-localization] descend it to a natural isomorphism on both localized good variables. This includes morphisms whose source and target have different filtration bounds.

source.place: Convolution graded comparison preceding Tag 0H7W (lemma-kunneth-converges), used in Tag 0H7Y (proposition-kunneth-filtered); localization as in Derived Categories Tag 05S2

proof.text: Apply the comparisons of Steps 7 and 8 to $(SU,SV)$ and use the counit $ES\simeq1$ of [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement]. Naturality of $\omega$ and $\operatorname{gr}^i$ gives $\omega ES\simeq\omega$ and $\operatorname{gr}^i ES\simeq\operatorname{gr}^i$, producing exactly both displayed isomorphisms of the statement for $U\star V$. Their formulas on good chain maps are those already fixed in Steps 7 and 8. To spell out naturality for denominators, an equation $F(w)\eta_X=\eta_YG(w)$ with $w\in W$ implies $F(w)^{-1}\eta_Y=\eta_XG(w)^{-1}$ by multiplying by the two inverses. Thus the representative naturality squares also commute for inverse denominators and then for every composite word of ordinary maps and inverse denominators in either variable. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] ensures that these are the descended comparisons, independently of the word representing a morphism. In particular the underlying map for a pair between good representatives is the ordinary derived tensor of the underlying maps, and all identity and composition laws persist.
